dvibhaṅga
(‘bent in two places’)
------------------------------------------
Images of gods and minor deities associated with them, especially in the standing posture may be sabhaṅga (with bends) or abhaṅga (without bends). An image which is द्विभङ्ग is bent in two places, one at the loins and the other at the neck. It is usual to show the images of goddesses in this posture, especially when they are with consorts and in the standing pose.

dvivedī
(‘one [who has studied] two वेदस्’)
------------------------------------------
Started perhaps as the academic title of a person who has studied two वेदस् (dvi = two) it gradually became the family title of persons born as his descendants.
Similarly is the evolution of the two other titles trivedī and caturvedī—for those who are the scions of the persons who had mastered three or four वेदस्.
Study of one Veda was the minimum expected of every द्विज or the twice-born.

dvīpa
(‘island’)
------------------------------------------
According to the ancient geography as depicted in some पुराणस् like the Viṣṇupurāṇa (2.2) this world (or earth) comprises seven dvīpas or continents, each surrounded by an ocean.
Bhāratavarṣa (India) is in the first continent called जम्बूद्वीप.
See SAPTADVĪPA for details.

dvija
(‘one [who is] born twice’)
------------------------------------------
Persons belonging to the first three varṇas or castes are called ‘dvijas’. Literally, the word means ‘One who is born a second time or twice-born’.
The first birth is the physical birth from the womb of the मोथेर्. The second is the spiritual birth brought about by the sacrament of उपनयन. Hence all those who have undergone the उपनयन ceremony—the ब्राह्मणस्, the kṣattriyas and the vaiśyas—are ‘dvijas’. However, in practice the term is more generally applied to the ब्राह्मणस्.
The ब्राह्मणस् of Vedic learning are called ‘vipras’ and the vipras with an excellent conduct are known as ‘śrotriyas’.
See also UPANAYANA.

dvitāla
(‘[measuring] two tālas’)
------------------------------------------
In the मूर्तिशिल्पशास्त्र or इचोनोग्रफ्य्, all the measurements are based on ताल (measurement of the length of the face, which is equal to the span) as the basic unit. The images and associated figures are to be made as per this tālamāna system.
The measurement of द्विताल (two tālas or spans, equal to 24 aṅgulas) is adopted while preparing the images of birds like swan, dwarfish spirits such as Kūṣmāṇḍa and for the मत्स्यावतार of विष्णु.
See TĀLAMĀNA SYSTEM for details.
